reasons.plausibility: Deep cryogenic treatment of a stable, disordered BCC refractory high-entropy alloy is unlikely to induce phase transitions or significantly enhance dislocation mobility at room temperature; the proposed mechanism contradicts the well-established stability of these alloys and lacks a clear physical basis for improving plasticity without compromising strength.
reasons.testability: The hypothesis proposes a clear comparative experiment with defined quantitative criteria (≥10% plastic strain increase, ≤5% yield strength loss) and microstructural characterization, making it falsifiable.
reasons.usefulness: The hypothesis is not useful because it proposes an intervention (deep cryogenic treatment) that is physically unsound for this class of alloys, diverting attention from more promising compositional or processing strategies.
